headline: Forest are 19th and losing — yet the market makes them favourites
summary: Nottingham Forest are 19th with 5 points and have lost three Premier League games in a row, yet the market makes them the side to win at Ipswich on Friday. The reason is what they create: Forest lost 1-3 at Crystal Palace despite 3.34 expected goals, and OneFootball reports Morgan Gibbs-White is fit. Ipswich pushed Manchester City to 2-3 on Saturday, so the game stays close. Forest are 42.7% to win, Ipswich's chance slipped from 30.8% to 29.5% in a day, and the market rates Forest 0.25 goals the stronger side, with 2.7 goals expected.
read: Nottingham Forest are 19th, on three straight defeats, and still the side the market rates to win at Portman Road — 42.7% to Ipswich's 29.5%. Their chance creation explains the price, and Glasner has Morgan Gibbs-White fit again for it.

facts.fact: Nottingham Forest are the favourites at Ipswich: 42.7% to Ipswich's 29.5%.
facts.meaning: The market has Forest more likely than not to avoid defeat and only about a quarter of a goal better on the handicap — a close game with a clear lean to the away side.

facts.fact: Oliver Glasner confirmed Morgan Gibbs-White is fit to face Ipswich — Forest's highest-rated player this season at 7.47.
facts.meaning: Forest's main creator, 540 minutes and three goal involvements this season, is available for the game that matters most to their season.

facts.fact: Nottingham Forest arrive on three straight Premier League defeats and sit 19th with 5 points from seven games.
facts.meaning: It is a side in the bottom three and losing every week — which is exactly the tension in this price.

facts.fact: Forest lost 1-3 at Crystal Palace despite generating 3.34 xG.
facts.meaning: They created enough to win comfortably and lost — the finishing, not the football, is the problem going into Friday.

facts.fact: Ipswich lost 3-2 at Manchester City on Saturday.
facts.meaning: Gary O'Neil's side scored twice at the champions and, according to reports, switched to a back three with two full-backs for stability — they arrive above Forest in the table.

facts.fact: Forest forward Igor Jesus is out with a calf injury after 316 minutes and one goal in six league appearances this season.
facts.meaning: Forest lose a rotation forward, thinning the attacking options behind Gibbs-White for a game they are expected to win.

facts.fact: Ipswich midfielder Svetozar Lukic is doubtful with a groin injury — 502 minutes in seven appearances this season, with one assist and a 6.7 rating.
facts.meaning: Ipswich risk losing a regular starter in midfield for the visit of the side the market rates to win.

facts.fact: The Athletic reports that defender Nikola Milenkovic should also be fit for Friday's game at Portman Road.
facts.meaning: Forest's defence looks close to full strength for a match where they will be asked to absorb home pressure.

sources.fact: Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner confirmed Morgan Gibbs-White is fit to face Ipswich Town on Friday.
The Athletic reports that defender Nikola Milenkovic should also be fit for Friday's Premier League game at Portman Road.
Nottingham Forest will bid to end a run of three straight defeats when they face Ipswich Town, according to the Nottingham Post.
Nottingham Forest lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal on Sunday, October 18, 2026, with Noni Madueke scoring a late deflected winner.
The Nottingham Post reports that Nottingham Forest are struggling to score goals and sit at the wrong end of the Premier League table.
Oliver Glasner struck an upbeat, defiant tone when he faced the media before Forest's trip to Ipswich, according to OneFootball.
Ipswich lost narrowly 3-2 at Manchester City on Saturday, a game in which fans said a switch by Gary O'Neil to three centre-backs alongside two full-backs gave the team stability.
Ipswich legend Terry Butcher told BBC Radio Suffolk that the Tractor Boys' players now understand the "power" of the Premier League.
